patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Lightspeed Retail and OpenCart share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Lightspeed Retail only if your buying job matches “Retail POS + omnichannel — Basic $89/mo, Core $149 highlighted, Plus $289/mo USD; Lightspe” rather than OpenCart's shape. Choose OpenCart only if your buying job matches “GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by” rather than Lightspeed Retail's shape. Workflow advantage: Lightspeed Retail leans omnichannel-retail; OpenCart leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Lightspeed Retail and OpenCart share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Lightspeed Retail is Retail POS + omnichannel — Basic $89/mo, Core $149 highlighted, Plus $289/mo USD; Lightspeed Payments ~1.5% card-present; eCommerce on highe; OpenCart is GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by secondary sources (confirm live). WooCommerce kee.
- Workflow coverage skew: Lightspeed Retail-leaning omnichannel-retail vs OpenCart-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Lightspeed Retail — No free plan or documented self-serve trial — contact sales is the common path; OpenCart — Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0.

Limitations — Lightspeed Retail: No free plan or documented self-serve trial — contact sales is the common path; Third-party payment processors may incur a high monthly surcharge versus Lightspeed Payments (~1.5% card-present) — confirm live; OpenCart: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0; Managed cloud floors are not first-party confirmed here — confirm live before budgeting.

Poor-fit cases: Lightspeed Retail is a poor fit when that limitation bites: No free plan or documented self-serve trial — contact sales is the common path · OpenCart is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0 · Avoid Lightspeed Retail if you actually need OpenCart's motion (GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
